title: docs(research): map selected BIT caller and storage obligations
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The bootstrap scope map is a 2026-10-14 snapshot, before the public first-range caller and all-size logical-caller proposal. Add a focused successor so contributors can find the current physical, time and outer-wrapper obligations without rebuilding published logical recursion.

```text
bottleneck brief / bootstrap map
  -> caller and storage map
     -> exact PR2697 and PR2753 source contracts
     -> seven component storage scopes
     -> physical placement, H2 and compatible-stock wrapper handoffs
```

The map distinguishes nonblank content, retained capacity and physical tape placement, explains which data bounds already include their component peaks, and preserves the earlier snapshot. This is navigation and scoped replay-route checking. It adopts no pending proof or supplier and changes no selected frontier.

## Task and overlap

Assigned `scope-navigation`, scope key `fff26335d457e528d9c4`, consolidation nonce `2bf15ca78266905dea72039c34fa99c5`, priority revision 5. Scope refined to the selected BIT caller/storage family and two entry links. Base canonical main `936fac15b1b1b59dc5285c713a77f9f3c07b2906`.

[Canonical claim in Discussion2319](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2319#discussioncomment-18958218). The map pins all nine full dependency heads through immutable source links, including PR2697 `a53fdf4bcbe33c6732f0bec1badc8c023380f9d1` and PR2753 `7dba5452a4071a856a0b11cebdcd2d3b6bcd7659`. It adds a navigation bridge to those results, not another implementation or sharper storage theorem. The ongoing physical numerical-bank claim remains separate. Final overlap covered 708 open PRs and 1,397 Discussion records with complete pagination at 20:40/20:42 UTC; canonical main and all nine heads were unchanged at 20:42 UTC.

## Validation

Before: the linked bootstrap snapshot ends with early implementation premises and no route to the newer complete logical caller. After: the new map resolves the exact callers, compatible stock, storage metrics and remaining boundaries.

On macOS 27.0.1 arm64 / CPython 3.12.15:

- All nine `scripts/research_package.py --package research/NAME --check-only` runs pass in separate pinned sparse worktrees.
- PR2753's `verify.py --suite recursion` passes against its exact retained receipt, including its rejected-return controls. Digest `6ab6832821d0ff9d3f71075c45894c2bbdbc6d16d7e47d8bac7e72a7e2ceed9e`.
- All 25 relative links in the three changed documents resolve; all 13 immutable source links resolve to their exact Git blobs. The documented exact-SHA fetch succeeds.
- `python -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'` passes 70 tests, three skipped. `git diff --check` passes.
- Separate read-only source/document review found no substantive scope or accounting issues.

No full package suites, selected GL64 Boolean payload, selected cold replay, physical compiler, formal-kernel or hosted CI result is claimed. Source/proof review and the finite recursion suite do not independently establish the pending parametric proofs.

## Credit

Jose Manuel/jmbarrancoml supplies the first-range caller and source/stream/hosting lineage; David Arias supplies the independent all-size logical caller. The component results retain individual credit to ywz65, starship-s and Nick Petalas. The older map retains Josie Elliston, ToikY and Adam Gall's implication/audit credit and the selected construction's attribution. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

The map gives bounded first steps for physical frame reuse, stronger H2 time contracts and compatible stock through the outer wrapper, with their blockers. These are follow-ups to public pending sources; no family expansion or maintainer adoption is inferred.

## Merge danger

Two-way documentation change, confined to three research guidance files. Frozen packages and selected records remain untouched.
